questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of Kubernetes NetworkPolicy default-deny behavior and namespace isolation.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics and default-deny
- Namespace isolation and namespace selectors
- Ingress vs Egress rules

## Code Example
```yaml
# policy.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-cross-namespace
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: tenant-a
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: tenant-a
```

```yaml
# compliant-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: p-a-compliant
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl
    image: curlimages/curl:8.88.0
    command: ["sh","-c","curl -s http://tenant-a-service.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local:80/health || true"]
```

```yaml
# noncompliant-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: p-a-cross
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl
    image: curlimages/curl:8.88.0
    command: ["sh","-c","curl -s http://tenant-b-service.tenant-b.svc.cluster.local:80/health || true"]
```

```bash
# verification plan
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f compliant-pod.yaml
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-pod.yaml
# test within tenant-a
kubectl logs p-a-compliant -n tenant-a
# cross-namespace should fail
kubectl logs p-a-cross -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for namespace-label-based multi-tenant isolation?
- What changes if using Calico instead of default k8s NetworkPolicy support?

```yaml
# Passing manifest: mtls STRICT and egress restricted
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: app
spec:

    mode: STRICT
```

```yaml

  name: bypass-mtls
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assess practical use of OPA in Kubernetes, translating security expectations into verifiable policies; tests demonstrate understanding of Pod spec structure.

## Key Concepts
- Rego fundamentals
- PodSpec fields: volumes.hostPath, securityContext.privileged, capabilities
- OPA test framework and unit tests
- Admission testing approaches

## Code Example
```javascript
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  some vol in input.request.object.spec.volumes
  vol.hostPath
  msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  some c in input.request.object.spec.containers
  c.securityContext.privileged == true
  msg := "privileged containers are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  some c in input.request.object.spec.containers
  some cap in c.securityContext.capabilities.add
  cap == "NET_ADMIN"
  msg := "NET_ADMIN capability is forbidden"
}
```

## Compliant Pod Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: false
      capabilities:
        add: []
  volumes:
  - name: config
    emptyDir: {}
```

## Noncompliant Pod Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
      capabilities:
        add: ["NET_ADMIN"]
  volumes:
  - name: host-root
    hostPath:
      path: /
```

## Validation Plan
1. Test policy with OPA: `opa test -v policy.rego`
2. Validate compliant pod: `kubectl apply -f compliant.yaml`
3. Verify noncompliant rejection: `kubectl apply -f noncompliant.yaml --dry-run=server`

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design scalable, enforceable policy gates across clouds with image provenance and hardening.

## Key Concepts
- Image provenance (Sigstore Cosign)
- SecurityContext: RunAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities.drop ALL
- RBAC: namespace scoping and least privilege
- Policy engines: Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- CI verification: cosign verify, dry-run manifests, local validation

## Code Example
```javascript
name: CI Gate
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify image signatures
        run: cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ env.IMAGE }}
      - name: Validate manifests (dry-run)
        run: kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f k8s/
```

```javascript
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "containers must set RunAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop:
                    - ALL
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy exceptions for service accounts used by CI workflows?
- How would you scale this policy across 100s of namespaces with different prod/stage gating?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world multi-tenant data platforms require strong admission control to enforce image provenance and host security postures across clouds. Gatekeeper with Rego enables centralized policy with testable manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint objects
- Image provenance: registry, non-latest, digest
- Pod hardening: resources, securityContext, privilegeEscalation
- Namespace labeling and admission scope
- CI validation: conftest, gatekeeper audit, sample manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (ImageProvenanceAndSecurity)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: imageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package imageprovenance
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          some i
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
          image := container.image
          startswith(image, "registry.example.com/")
          not endswith(image, ":latest")
```

- **SBOM Attestation**: Software Bill of Materials provides transparency into image contents and dependencies
- **GitHub Actions Workflows**: Implementing gates and policy checks in CI/CD pipelines
- **Registry Allowlist**: Restricting deployments to approved registries prevents supply chain attacks

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Docker Security Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Validate Dockerfile
        run: |
          # Check for non-root USER
          grep -q 'USER ' Dockerfile || exit 1
          # Check for multi-stage build
          grep -q 'FROM.*AS' Dockerfile || exit 1
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json > sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign image and SBOM with Cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
          cosign attest --type spdx-json --predicate sbom.json ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Verify signature and attestation
        run: |
          cosign verify ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
```

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes admission control

- Node labeling and NodeAffinity

## Code Example
```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sketch (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: gputypematch
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: GPUsTypeConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package gputypematch
      violation["msg"] = msg :-
        input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
        and some container in input.review.object.spec.containers
        and container.resources.requests["nvidia.com/gpu"] > 0
        and not input.review.object.spec.nodeSelector["gpuType"] in allowed_types
        and not input.review.object.metadata.namespace in namespace_allowlist
        msg := "GPU type not allowed in namespace"
```
